name: Methuselah
overview: Methuselah was a male figure in the early biblical genealogy, uniquely identified as the son of Enoch according to Genesis 5:21. Beyond this, Scripture does not specify his tribe or additional personal details. His role is primarily genealogical and symbolic within the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Methuselah is a proper name found in Genesis 5:21 and is understood to mean 'man of the javelin.' This meaning is not stated as given by God but reflects the Hebrew origin of the name.
familyAndRelationships: Methuselah is recorded as the son of Enoch, as noted in Genesis 5:21, and the father of Lamech, according to Genesis 5:25. These relationships place him within the direct lineage leading to Noah.
scriptureSignificance: Methuselah's significance lies in his extraordinary lifespan, which is noted as the longest recorded in Scripture at 969 years. His life symbolizes God's patience and longsuffering, as his death coincided with the year of the Flood, marking a critical moment of divine judgment and mercy in the biblical account.
